Community matrix ordered by phylogenetic beta diversity

Source: R/plots.R
plot_phylo_beta.Rd

The heatmap that Peres-Neto & Kembel (2015) suggest for phylo_beta_test(): sites follow an axis of the matrix predicted by the environment and species follow the tree, so that a link between environment and phylogeny appears as clades that replace each other along the sites.

Usage

plot_phylo_beta(x, comm, tree, axis = 1, col = "#0072B2", cex = 0.7, ...)

Arguments

x

Result of phylo_beta_test().

comm

The community matrix given to phylo_beta_test().

tree

The phylo object given to phylo_beta_test().

axis

Axis of x$scores that orders the sites.

col

Colour of the largest value, with white for absences.

cex

Size of the text.

...

Passed to graphics::image().

Value

The ordered matrix, invisibly.

References

Peres-Neto, P. R., & Kembel, S. W. (2015). Phylogenetic gradient analysis: environmental drivers of phylogenetic variation across ecological communities. Plant Ecology, 216, 709–724. doi:10.1007/s11258-014-0405-0

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
traits <- species_traits(tree, lambda = 1, optima_range = c(-1, 101),
                         rmax_range = c(0, 30))
env <- runif(50, 0, 100)
comm <- simulate_static(traits, env, incidence = TRUE)$abundance
keep <- rowSums(comm) > 0
out <- phylo_beta_test(comm[keep, ], tree, env[keep], n_perm = 9)
plot_phylo_beta(out, comm[keep, ], tree)
